design.quote: In this scoping review, we summarise the existing literature on the concomitant use of conventional ADs with classic psychedelics in humans with the aims to assess safety, tolerability, efficacy, and subjective effects.
design.text: A scoping review of existing literature on the concomitant use of conventional antidepressants and classic psychedelics in humans.

findings.quote: The main findings indicate that this combination appears generally safe and tolerable with no robust evidence of increased risk for serotonin toxicity or syndrome.
findings.text: The combination of antidepressants and classic psychedelics appears generally safe and tolerable with no robust evidence of an increased risk for serotonin toxicity or syndrome.
findings.second_hand: The main findings indicate that this combination appears generally safe and tolerable with no robust evidence of increased risk for serotonin toxicity or syndrome.

findings.quote: A final observation was the potential attenuation of acute subjective effects of psychedelics, although other studies did not show this.
findings.text: Antidepressants may potentially attenuate the acute subjective effects of psychedelics, although other studies did not show this effect.

findings.quote: Ten studies evaluating the safety of the concomitant use of ADs and classic psychedelics showed no signs of serotonin toxicity or syndrome.
findings.text: Ten studies evaluating the safety of using antidepressants and classic psychedelics together showed no signs of serotonin toxicity or syndrome.

limits.quote: the complex interplay between specific dosages of ADs and classic psychedelics remains poorly understood, necessitating controlled studies to elucidate specific dose-response relationships and the distinct effects of particular AD classes.
limits.text: The relationship between specific dosages of antidepressants and classic psychedelics is not well understood and requires further controlled study.
